question: Does the original UI56 10000ms post-Refresh heading assertion originate in a recovered human latency requirement, or only later agent policy; would awaiting the exact operation response before the same matcher preserve its gate?

findings.interpretation: No direct human instruction imposing a UI56 ten-second SLA was recovered in the bounded sources. Positive original project records deliberately evaluate Refresh-to-visible readiness against ten seconds, including prior failures, a9955ms trace and a subsequent clean pass. Moving the matcher start after a response changes that temporal criterion; identical matcher text or global timeout is insufficient to call it the unchanged gate.

temporalReasoning.original: The heading assertion starts immediately after the click returns and allows up to10000ms for visibility.
temporalReasoning.proposedSequentialResponseWait: An operation-response wait would precede the10000ms matcher; elapsed readiness acceptance becomes response-wait time plus matcher time.
temporalReasoning.diagnosticAlternative: A response observer can be armed without delaying the original matcher. That adds information without substituting a later-starting temporal oracle.
temporalReasoning.legitimateTestFixCaveat: A separately justified correction to a test contract may be an engineering task, but this receipt does not approve a changed acceptance contract or classify a delayed matcher as the unchanged original gate.
